items.title: Free tutorial: Design Mechs in VR Using Substance 3D Modeler
items.excerpt: The Gnomon Workshop released a free 30-minute tutorial in which concept artist Andre-Lang Huynh designs a mech entirely inside VR with Substance 3D Modeler, then finishes in KeyShot. It is a concrete argument for sculpting hard-surface concepts in headset rather than on a mouse.

items.title: New CG software you may have missed: 9 August 2026
items.excerpt: This week's smaller releases include FumeFX 7.6 with a multigrid PCG solver and Fast Upres, Character Control Rig 0.3.1 for Blender with a new retargeting engine, and PFTrack 26.08. The quiet tier of the pipeline is where most production speedups actually land.

items.title: How to Create Hair and Feathers for an Owl Harpy Character
items.excerpt: Eugenia Zanina walks through building an Owl Harpy's hair and feathers in XGen with a custom shader, finishing with lighting in Unreal Engine 5.5. A reminder of how much of character craft still lives in grooming decisions no generator makes for you.

items.title: Check Out This Cute Blender Animation of the Viral Milk Face Kitten
items.excerpt: 3D artist Vossadova rebuilt the viral milk-faced kitten meme as a stylized Blender animation. A small case study in how hand-made 3D still wins attention against an internet full of generated riffs on the same meme.

items.title: How I Cut UX Review Cycles 30% with an AI Agent
items.excerpt: A build log for a custom review agent that catches the UI details a human reviewer skims past — spacing drift, missing states, inconsistent components — before the design review meeting. The claim is a 30% shorter review loop on a Flutter product.

items.title: Teaching Your AI Web Design Some Actual Taste
items.excerpt: Models default to the statistical center of the web, so the author stops waiting for a better model and instead writes taste down: type scale, spacing rhythm, restraint rules, plus multiple options per prompt instead of one-shot output.

items.title: Giving your AI agent eyes on your design specs: The Lanhu MCP approach
items.excerpt: Rather than screenshotting a spec into a prompt, this wires an MCP server that hands the agent the actual design layers, tokens and reviewer comments. The agent can then audit its own output against the spec instead of guessing from pixels.

items.title: Thinking outside the box (literally)
items.excerpt: An argument that language models have saturated the digital box and the next design frontier is physical: world models, embodied agents, products that have to act in a room. It reframes what a designer's canvas is about to become.

items.title: What Star Trek got wrong about AI (so far)
items.excerpt: Fluent conversation arrived decades early while reliability did not, and the singular shipboard computer turned out to be infinitely copyable. A useful corrective for teams still designing AI features around a sci-fi mental model.

items.title: The cybernetic application
items.excerpt: Applying Stafford Beer's viable systems theory to AI-era products: the app is a feedback loop between user, model and interface rather than a stack of screens. It changes what the designer is actually shaping.

items.title: The Square Enix AI fiasco convinces me we all need to start documenting our creative process
items.excerpt: After Square Enix's AI accusation cycle, the argument is blunt: keeping your sketches, drafts and version history may soon be the only way to prove a human made the work. Process documentation becomes a professional defence, not housekeeping.

items.title: So, it seems Disney music is our only protection against Meta's pervert glasses
items.excerpt: Copyright takedowns, not privacy design, are what currently stops always-on camera glasses from recording you. A sharp look at how little interface-level consent design exists in the smart-glasses category.

items.title: Vermont's logo looks like it was made in five seconds... so why do I love it?
items.excerpt: A defence of a state logo that reads as effortless — and a useful test case for the new reflex of dismissing anything that looks fast or machine-made. Perceived effort is now part of how identity work gets judged.

items.title: How to use Claude's voice mode
items.excerpt: Claude's voice mode now runs on Sonnet and Opus with 14 languages and connected-app access, turning the assistant into a hands-free front end for work already wired into your tools. Voice becomes another surface designers have to spec.

items.title: How to use ChatGPT's new, more natural Voice Mode for conversations
items.excerpt: GPT-Live's full-duplex architecture lets ChatGPT listen and speak at once, backchanneling 'mhmm' while you talk. Overlapping turn-taking is a genuinely new interaction pattern to design around, not just a faster TTS.

items.title: Supernatural's head of fitness on rebooting the VR exercise app after leaving Meta
items.excerpt: Leanne Pedante describes rebuilding Supernatural's coaching, pacing and embodiment design as an independent company. A rare candid account of designing for the body in headset rather than for a screen.

items.title: Using and Styling the Dialog Element
items.excerpt: A full pass over the native <dialog> element — showModal() versus show(), backdrop styling, focus management and animation. The exact component-level detail agent-generated UIs keep getting wrong.

items.title: How Baseline Can Help You Ship Less JavaScript
items.excerpt: Auditing dependencies against Baseline feature status can strip 60–90KB of gzipped code that browsers now handle natively. A concrete way to stop agents and templates from bolting on libraries the platform already replaced.
